question: does the binary UP-vs-DOWN target on all 44 context features beat its own majority out-of-sample with a converged class-balanced fit?
whyNotARerun: every prior out-of-sample run on this cache carried the three-class label20 target; no prior run dropped FLAT and scored UP-vs-DOWN out-of-sample. v2 is not a rerun of that family either: it corrects binary-context-v1's three-output fit and its mis-named mixes

correctionOf.defect: v1 fitted this two-class target with three output columns, because fit_weighted sized its matrix from len(CLASSES) == 3. Labels {0,1} used columns 0 and 1, the column CLASSES calls UP never received a target row, and predictedMix/actualMix indexed into CLASSES so the binary positive class was written out as FLAT while UP was written as 0 on every fold.
correctionOf.scope: correctness repair of the model output dimension and of the reported class names only; criteria, thresholds and protocol untouched
correctionOf.exposure: these calendar years were previously examined by v1 and by every earlier run on this cache, so this corrected run re-measures an already-observed holdout and is not a pristine independent result. No threshold was changed after any metric was seen.

target.label: binary UP vs DOWN, FLAT dropped
target.encodingNote: BINARY_CLASSES[1] is UP and is reported as UP; the cache's three-class FLAT rows are dropped before encoding

model.optimizer: fit_weighted imported from balanced_experiment, called with classes=BINARY_CLASSES so the matrix is built for two outputs
model.corrects: binary-context-v1's three-column fit on a two-class target
model.classWeights: n / (2 * n_c) over the two classes present, normalised to mean 1 inside fit_weighted

protocol.folds: baseline_experiment's rule: one fold per test year 2021..2026
protocol.standardisation: training-fold mean and standard deviation only
protocol.uncertainty: moving-block bootstrap over decision dates, 20-date blocks, 400 resamples, candidate minus shuffled control

criteriaSource: fixed in this docstring before any number from this run was seen

summary.inSampleBoundNote: signal_floor's in-sample binary/44 over-majority, measured by the corrected two-class cell; a holdout number is expected to be smaller, not larger
summary.inSampleBoundV1Note: the same bound as measured by the historical three-column construction, kept for disclosure; its reported mix summed to the row count, so no column-2 prediction occurred even though the third logit was trained

regimeClause: reported, not a pass criterion; a regime with >= 1000 rows and margin <= -0.05 is named in the verdict
fidelityLimitations: the cache carries no dataQuality mask, so the quarantine balanced_experiment applies cannot be reproduced here
crypto only: one market, 93,452 rows in the cache
this holdout was examined by binary-context-v1 and is re-measured here, so it is a correction of an observed result, not a fresh independent one
verdict: NO-GO: C1_meanMarginPositive, C2_foldsWon, C3_noDegenerateFold, C4_controlIntervalExcludesZero, C5_worstFoldMargin failed the criteria fixed before this run. Qualification: adverse in 2020-22 recovery, 2022-26 advance.
nextQuestion: the generalisation gap itself: what changes the margin, given the in-sample bound says the separation is present
notAPromotion: a passing verdict is a candidate for reproduction, never a GO
